prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from TokenStorage never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired stored token as valid and the proactive silent-refresh path is skipped, forcing a full interactive re-authorization on every restart once the access token has expired. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from TokenStorage never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired stored token as valid and the proactive silent-refresh path is skipped, forcing a full interactive re-authorization on every restart once the access token has expired. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes the root cause directly in _initialize(): calls context.update_token_expiry() when the loaded token has expires_in, a 7-line change with a dedicated expired_tokens fixture and unit test. #2875's own inline comment names this exact token_expiry_time bug as the reason it needs a new 'Step 3.5' branch in async_auth_flow that tries a stored refresh_token before full re-auth — but that only patches the symptom at the 401 handler; any other code path that calls is_token_valid() before this branch runs (e.g. a proactive pre-request check) still gets a wrong answer, and the extra branch adds more surface area to an already complex async_auth_flow for no added coverage once #1784 is applied.

prs.author: adityuhkapoor

(2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same function, `pre_parse_json` in func_metadata.py, to stop it from JSON-decoding string values for fields whose annotation is a union that includes `str` (e.g. `str | None`), which was silently corrupting plain strings that happen to look like JSON (e.g. the literal string "null" or a numeric string being turned into `None`/an int instead of staying a string). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` generalizes the fix to any union composed solely of simple scalar types (str, int, float, bool, None), so it also covers `int | None`, `float | None`, `bool | None`, etc., not just `str | None`. #3056's `_is_optional_str` only special-cases the exact `str | None` shape (with `_unwrap_annotated` to see through one level of `Annotated` on a union member), so it's strictly narrower in the set of annotations it fixes. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the StreamableHTTP client's SSE reconnection loop in `_handle_reconnection` exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the code currently just logs and returns — the in-flight request that triggered reconnection is left hanging forever with no error ever delivered to the caller. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 resolves the hang at the protocol layer: it builds a JSONRPCError keyed to the specific pending request's id and sends it through ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the affected request is unblocked while the rest of the session keeps running; it also upgrades the log line from logger.debug to logger.warning, and changes the branch's pragma from '# pragma: no cover' to '# pragma: no branch', indicating the new code path is now covered by a test. #3098's diff (as shown) only adds a generic _unwrap_exception helper that digs a StreamableHTTPError out of anyio ExceptionGroups so it can be raised — a coarser fix that would propagate an exception up through the task group and fail the whole client session rather than just the one outstanding request, and includes no corresponding pragma/test changes in the diff.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add near-identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic (compare _iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041 — same char-by-char state machine). #3041 additionally layers a scheme-aware extraction step (_extract_bearer_auth_params) that splits the full header into per-challenge segments and only collects params belonging to the Bearer challenge, which correctly handles a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Digest realm="x", Bearer realm="y"'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead splits everything after the header's first space as one flat param list, which does not disambiguate params belonging to a different, non-Bearer scheme in the same header value — a case #3041 explicitly handles.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add near-identical quote/escape-aware comma-splitting logic (compare _iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041 — same char-by-char state machine). #3041 additionally layers a scheme-aware extraction step (_extract_bearer_auth_params) that splits the full header into per-challenge segments and only collects params belonging to the Bearer challenge, which correctly handles a header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Digest realm="x", Bearer realm="y"'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead splits everything after the header's first space as one flat param list, which does not disambiguate params belonging to a different, non-Bearer scheme in the same header value — a case #3041 explicitly handles.

members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: parsing the WWW-Authenticate header value naively (via substring/plain-comma matching) causes false positives when a quoted parameter value itself contains a comma or a substring that looks like another parameter name. Both introduce a quote-aware, backslash-escape-aware comma splitter to properly tokenize auth-params before matching.
